title: Inverse image of sheaves of sets along a composite of continuous maps
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be continuous maps of topological spaces, and for a continuous map $h$ let $h^{-1}$ be the inverse image of sheaves of sets, left adjoint to the direct image $h_*$, with unit $\eta^h$ given on sections by $\eta^h_{\mathcal G,W}:\mathcal G(W)\to(h^{-1}\mathcal G)(h^{-1}W)$, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $Z$ there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of sets $c_{\mathcal G}:f^{-1}g^{-1}\mathcal G\to(g\circ f)^{-1}\mathcal G$ on $X$ such that $c_{\mathcal G,(g\circ f)^{-1}W}\bigl(\eta^f_{g^{-1}\mathcal G,g^{-1}W}(\eta^g_{\mathcal G,W}(s))\bigr)=\eta^{g\circ f}_{\mathcal G,W}(s)$ for every open $W\subseteq Z$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(W)$; it is an isomorphism, and natural in $\mathcal G$.

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma Tag 008I (label lemma-pullback-composition, line 2209): '(g o f)^{-1} and f^{-1} o g^{-1} are canonically isomorphic' (both left adjoint to (g o f)_* = g_* o f_*, Lemma lemma-pushforward-composition); the description by units is that of the isomorphism of left adjoints
